quiz.question: Why can digital signals tolerate small amounts of noise?

answers.answer: Digital signals are transmitted at higher voltages than analog signals
A slightly wobbly high is still clearly recognized as high
Digital signals use special wires that block all interference
Noise only affects analog signals due to their lower frequency

quiz.explanation: Since a digital signal only needs to be recognized as high or low, small amounts of noise barely matter. A slightly wobbly 'high' is still clearly 'high,' giving digital signals a built-in safety margin that analog signals lack.

quiz.question: What happens when noise is added to an analog signal?

answers.answer: The noise is filtered out by the receiving device
The noise permanently distorts the information
The signal switches to digital mode for protection

quiz.explanation: An analog signal has no safety net. Any noise added to it permanently distorts the information because you cannot tell the original value from the interference, because the noise becomes part of the signal.

quiz.question: In a noisy environment, which type of signal stays more readable?

answers.answer: Analog, because it can absorb noise into its smooth curve
Both are equally affected by noise
Digital, because it only needs to distinguish between two states
Neither: all signals fail in noisy environments

quiz.explanation: Digital signals stay readable in noisy environments because they only need to be recognized as one of two states (high or low). Small disturbances do not push the signal past the threshold between states, so the information survives intact.
